answers.q1: Cargo (Rust). The workspace requires Rust 1.96 (`rust-version = "1.96"` in Cargo.toml). Install dependencies with `cargo fetch` from the repository root; `cargo build --workspace` also works and fetches them.
answers.q2: `cargo test --workspace` runs the whole suite. CI also runs `cargo test --workspace --features unstable-index` and `cargo test --workspace --features pcre2`, so run those too to match CI.
answers.q3: `cargo test --test integration regression::`. Cargo.toml sets `autotests = false` and registers only the `integration` target (tests/tests.rs), which pulls in tests/regression.rs via `mod regression;`, so the file cannot be run as its own target. The `regression::` filter selects its tests.
answers.q4: `cargo fmt --all --check` (the CI rustfmt job). The CI docs job also runs `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items --workspace`. CI does not run clippy.
answers.q5: Cargo.lock and fuzz/Cargo.lock are cargo-managed and should only change through cargo commands. The man page and shell completions are generated by build.rs and not committed (the deployment/ directory is created at packaging time), so do not hand-edit them. There is no vendor/ directory. benchsuite/runs/ holds recorded benchmark output and is not hand-edited.

q1.reason: Identifies Cargo, rust-version 1.96, and gives `cargo fetch` / `cargo build` which match the accept criteria.

q2.reason: `cargo test --workspace` matches the accept criteria; the extra CI feature runs are harmless detail.

q3.reason: `cargo test --test integration regression::` is an accepted command and the explanation matches the truth.

q4.reason: Gives `cargo fmt --all --check`, correctly notes the cargo doc job, and correctly states CI does not run clippy.

q5.reason: Names Cargo.lock as tool-managed and says there is no vendor/ directory; the claims about generated man pages and benchsuite/runs do not contradict the truth or match a REJECT item (which lists only crates/*, tests/data, pkg/).
